approach: Root cause: an executable is written and run in the same process while a write handle (or a forked child that copied it) still holds the file. Four earlier jobs guarded the last symptom. Every test stand-in already goes through athena_testkit::write_executable except the `script` helper in slot_exec.rs unit tests, so the fix has four parts. (1) Widen the scan in no_in_process_exec_writes.rs: whole-identifier wrapper detection (a fn whose body holds a raw permission call and no write-bit expression, called from test code in the same file, or pub/pub(crate) from another file) and a chmod-in-argument rule (`sh -c`, .arg/.args, split Command::new), skipping a full multi-line write_executable( call, with fixtures that fail on both and pass on the helper. (2) Convert the slot_exec.rs `script` helper and drop its EXEMPT entry. (3) Move the ETXTBSY retry out of claude.rs into the neutral athena_agent::procs module (pub retry_busy plus retry_busy_with, 20 x 50 ms, libc::ETXTBSY only) and use it at every production site whose tests feed it a stand-in: claude.rs (2 sites), checks.rs run_check, reading.rs BinaryChecker::check, gh/transport.rs GhCli::gh, run/mod.rs run_bounded, slot_exec.rs real-cargo status; xtask gets its own std-only copy (no athena-agent edge, no Cargo.toml edit). (4) Record it: CHANGELOG Fixed entry whose first sentence is the root cause, D163 with the site table, a D160->D163 link placed after the D158->D162 link. This round answers critic findings 1-6: the athena-core run sites are now retried (athena-core already depends on athena-agent, Cargo.toml line 12), wrapper matching is by whole identifier and raw call, the multi-line helper call is skipped, the decisions.rs CHANGELOG reader is a dependent, the retry lives in procs, and the link order is fixed.

decisions.choice: Wrapper detection by whole identifier and raw call. A fn is a wrapper when its body (brace-counted) contains a raw permission call (`set_permissions(`, `from_mode(`, `.set_mode(`, or an OpenOptions `.mode(` with an argument) or a chmod-argument line, and contains no write-bit expression (`| 0o200`, `| 0o222`, `& !0o200`, `& !0o222`, whitespace-normalised, or `set_readonly(`). A body that only calls a function named set_executable is not a wrapper. A call is the name at an identifier boundary (previous char not alphanumeric, `_`, `.`), followed by `(`, on a test-region non-comment line that is not the `fn` line. Any same-file fn counts; a pub or pub(crate) fn counts in every file; fns under crates/athena-testkit/src/ are skipped.
decisions.reason: Finding 2. The write-bit exclusion keys on the mode expression, not any keyword in the body: the toggles in pin.rs:186-191, core/snapshot.rs:188-192 and git/snapshot.rs:440-445 all use `| 0o200` / `& !0o222`, so they are not wrappers. toolconfig.rs set_executable (private, line 15) and apply_base_tool_config (calls it) are not shared wrappers, so a future test calling apply_base_tool_config is not flagged for a stand-in it does not write. Identifier-boundary matching means a single-letter wrapper `t` is not found inside `format(` or `x.t(`. A fixture pins this.

rejected.why: A one-letter wrapper would match inside unrelated calls.

rejected.option: Exclude wrappers by a keyword anywhere in the body
rejected.why: A body that sets 0o755 and mentions 0o222 in a comment or other line would escape.
A new dependency for a lint over a few shapes; D160 chose a text scan, and the limits go in D163.

Lines inside a write_executable( call are skipped from the opening line to its closing paren (paren depth counted outside ordinary string literals, capped at 40 lines).

risks.risk: The wrapper rule flags a legitimate test call (a read-only toggle, a shared name used by an unrelated fn).
risks.mitigation: Raw-call and write-bit-expression tests, identifier-boundary matching, pub-only cross-file wrappers and skipping athena-testkit/src. Fixtures pin the write-bit toggle, the one-letter name and the private-not-flagged case, and the real-tree test shows the result. A hit is fixed or given a documented EXEMPT entry, never silently loosened.

risks.risk: The chmod rule misses a split form or flags a policy string or helper script body.
risks.mitigation: The rule needs the word chmod plus a command-building marker on the same line, a quoted "-c", and skips whole write_executable( calls. Fixtures cover a policy array, `git -c`, and a multi-line helper call. D163's Tradeoff states the text-scan limits (a script held in a variable and passed later is not seen).

risks.risk: The retry masks a real fault or slows a failing run.
risks.mitigation: At most 20 attempts of 50 ms (about 1 s), only on libc::ETXTBSY; the last error is returned unchanged; other errors return at once. Unit tests pin the bound and the pass-through.

risks.risk: A re-used Command whose stdio or pre_exec settings are consumed on a failed spawn (run_check sets stdout/stderr files and isolate()).
risks.mitigation: A std Command can be spawned again after a failed spawn and keeps its settings, including a Stdio::from(File) set before the first spawn. The producer builds `let mut cmd` first and wraps only the final spawn/output/status in the closure; the compiler and the existing tests check it. checks.rs keeps its per-error note.

risks.risk: Wrong line number or order in the new link, or a malformed entry, fails backtest or DecisionEntries.
risks.mitigation: D163 is appended last so earlier lines do not shift; the link goes after line 199 of the links file; the producer reads the link line from Grep -n 'Amends D160' docs/decisions.md after the final edit and runs the backtest, mirrors and decisions tests.

risks.risk: Making athena-core import athena_agent::procs for a helper adds coupling.
risks.mitigation: Both crates already depend on athena-agent, and retry_busy is a plain fn with no other state. The producer confirms with cargo build before the tests.

risks.risk: The introspection record records/introspections/2026-11/20261106-104005-m047.json is not in the planner's copy, so its proposed_request was not checked.
risks.mitigation: The reading is based on the request text and the code. The producer must not edit the record, and D163 cites the request, not the record.

risks.mitigation: The tree scan, the stress test (0 busy files through the helper) and the scan's ban on in-process writes keep the window closed; the retry is a second layer.

demonstrations.method: Read the new Fixed entry at the top of [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md and check its first sentence, then run the existing root-cause reader so the Unreleased section still parses.
demonstrations.observes: Grep -n 'while a write handle' CHANGELOG.md finds the new entry, whose first sentence says an executable is written and run in the same process while a write handle or forked child still holds it; the rest names the helper, the widened scan, the retry sites and D163. the_root_cause_is_named_in_the_changelog_and_the_log (decisions.rs:511) still passes because no existing Unreleased text was changed.

demonstrations.method: Read D163 and compare its site table with a fresh Grep for set_permissions|from_mode|set_mode|set_executable|chmod|\.mode\( over crates/*/{src,tests} and xtask; the decision-log mirror rules need the Provenance bullet.
demonstrations.observes: Every Grep hit has a row marked converted (slot_exec.rs test helper), retried (the run sites), or non-stand-in/exempt (toolconfig.rs, pin.rs, core/snapshot.rs, git/snapshot.rs, xtask set_executable, policy.rs and cap-change lib.rs string inputs, stand_in_stress.rs, the scan file, the helper); the tests pass.

demonstrations.method: Run the real-tree scan, which applies the widened rules to every file, then Grep the primitives.
demonstrations.observes: no_in_process_exec_writes and every_exemption_still_exists_and_still_has_a_hit pass with EXEMPT holding two entries (the scan file and the stress control). Grep for the five primitives shows only the helper, those two exemptions, and the documented non-stand-in production uses.

demonstrations.method: Grep retry_busy at each run site, and run the retry unit tests, including a kernel-level one: a stand-in written with write_executable is held open for writing by the test, a thread releases it after about 100 ms, and retry_busy(|| Command::new(&path).status()) succeeds.
demonstrations.observes: retry_busy is called in claude.rs (2 sites), checks.rs run_check, reading.rs BinaryChecker::check, gh/transport.rs GhCli::gh, run/mod.rs run_bounded, slot_exec.rs, and xtask found and check_credentials. Tests show success after N busy errors, a stop at the 20-attempt bound with the busy error returned, an immediate return on any other error, and success after a real held-open file is released.

demonstrations.method: Read the new fixture tests in the scan file.
demonstrations.observes: Fixtures for a pub wrapper above #[cfg(test)] called from test code; a test-only wrapper and its call; a cross-file pub wrapper through violations_with with the same fn private not flagged; a one-letter wrapper `t` where only the true call is flagged; `sh -c` with a chmod string; .arg("chmod"); .args(["-c", "chmod +x t"]); the split `Command::new(` then `"chmod"`; and not-flagged fixtures for a single-line and a multi-line write_executable call (script line mentions chmod), a 0o222 write-bit toggle fn, a `git -c` shell string, and a policy-style `["chmod +x src/lib.rs"]` array.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole testkit package. The fixtures are literal strings passed to the scan; the tree test passes the repository's own files.
demonstrations.observes: The wrapper and chmod fixtures return the expected (line, reason) hits; the helper, multi-line helper, write-bit and policy-array fixtures return none; the real-tree test passes; the stress test's helper variant meets 0 busy files.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without wrapper detection, the wrapper-call, test-only-wrapper, cross-file and one-letter fixtures get an empty hit list and fail their assertions. Without the chmod rule, the shell-string, .arg, .args and split-Command fixtures fail. If the rules over-reached, the helper, multi-line helper, write-bit, `git -c` and policy-array fixtures (asserted empty) and the real-tree test would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `violations_with(rel, text, shared)` and `violations(rel, text)` in crates/athena-testkit/tests/no_in_process_exec_writes.rs, plus `tree()` for the real files. `violations` and `tree` exist today (read at lines 73 and 127); `violations_with` and the wrapper collector are added by plan steps 6-8. Fixtures are literal strings passed as arguments; there is no double, the scan is the logic under test.

demonstrations.method: Run the full workspace suite, as the Athena test check does.
demonstrations.observes: All packages pass, including stand_in_stress, the exemption-staleness test, athena-cli backtest, mirrors and decisions tests, xtask policy and shard tests, slot_exec unit and integration tests (including the 0o644 case), the checks.rs run_check tests that run a fake cargo, the reading.rs stub_binary tests, and the claude.rs tests that run a stand-in through the retried sites.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the slot_exec.rs helper conversion, dropping its EXEMPT entry makes the scan test fail on that file. Without the procs retry_busy being pub, claude.rs, checks.rs, reading.rs, transport.rs, run/mod.rs and slot_exec.rs do not compile. A retry that swallowed non-busy errors would fail the retry unit tests, and one that never stopped would fail the bound test.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `athena_agent::procs::retry_busy` through claude_version and the driver spawn, `checks::run_check`, `BinaryChecker::check`, `GhCli::gh`, `run_bounded`, `slot_exec::run`, and xtask `found`. Existing tests drive them with stand-ins written by athena_testkit::write_executable (claude.rs tests, checks.rs:1003, reading.rs:9857, tests/slot_exec.rs, reconcile.rs:134, xtask main.rs:835); that seam exists today. The bound is unit-tested through `retry_busy_with` (added by plan step 2) with a closure that only counts calls and returns io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::ETXTBSY) N times; the retry loop is not in the closure.

demonstrations.method: Run the two Athena checks on the whole workspace after `cargo fmt --all`.
demonstrations.observes: Exit 0 with no diagnostics; `cargo fmt --all --check` is also clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unformatted edit fails fmt --check; a leftover private retry_busy in claude.rs, an unused import (Duration, libc) or a function left unused after the move fails clippy -D warnings; an unused PermissionsExt import after the slot_exec.rs conversion fails clippy.
demonstrations.seam: The checks themselves are the entry point: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check over the workspace, with the repository's lint configuration as-is and no double. The seam exists today; the plan edits only code the checks already cover.

demonstrations.method: Confirm neither D08-governed path is in the diff, then run the decision-log tests that check the D160 link.
demonstrations.observes: crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs do not appear (run/mod.rs is not a D08 path), so no D08 entry or link is needed; D163 says so. `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test backtest` passes with the new D160->D163 link at the line of 'Amends D160', placed after the D158->D162 link. If a D08 path was edited after all, D163 gains an 'Amends D08' line and a [[link]] older D08 newer D163.

demonstrations.method: Run the real-tree scan under the widened rules and read the count D163 states.
demonstrations.observes: Zero flagged lines outside EXEMPT, so 0 current files are newly refused. This is an expectation from a Grep read (the word chmod appears only in policy.rs string inputs, cap-change lib.rs:175 and the testkit helper); only the run settles it. D163 states 0% newly refused over the current tree and that no past readings are replayed.

demonstrations.method: Review the changed-file list and run the suite.
demonstrations.observes: Only CHANGELOG.md, the scan file, docs/decisions.md, docs/decision-links.toml, xtask/src/main.rs, and the Rust files with a retry or conversion (procs.rs, claude.rs, checks.rs, reading.rs, gh/transport.rs, run/mod.rs, slot_exec.rs) plus a doc line in athena-testkit/src/lib.rs change. No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, Cargo.toml or records/ change. The retry changes only the outcome of a run that failed with ETXTBSY.
